newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Richter Q1 margins up on strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: Richter Q1 margins up on strong dollar.

text.p: A strong U.S. dollar helped Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Richter Gedeon Rt to boost its margins in the first quarter of 1997, but it said a tight control of operating costs remains essential.

"Gross profit margins increased to 64.2 percent (in January-March 1997) from 62 percent in the corresponding period of the prior year, reflecting the favourable impact of a considerably stronger US dollar, and a change in the sales mix," Richter said in its earnings report.
Richter's Q1 earnings report was published in the official gazette of the Budapest Stock Exchange on Tuesday.
"Operating margins for the first quarter of 1997 were 33.8 percent compared with 28.6 percents in the corresponding period of 1996," the report said.

"The improvement results from a significant proportion of sales being invoiced in US dollar while incurring operating expenses in Hungarian forint, a devaluing currency, together with tight control on expenses and a management focus on achieving enhances operating efficiency."

Richter reported a net profit of 4.997 billion forints ($27.4 million) on sales of 12.801 billion forints in the first three months of 1997, up from a net profit of 3.258 billion forints on sales of 9.419 billion in the same period of 1996.
Of Richter's total sales, 8.272 billion forints were generated by exports.

"It is expected that as the year progresses, increases in salaries and other costs will negatively impact operating margins and result in lower levels than those reported in this first quarter," the report said.
-- Emese Bartha, Budapest newsroom +36 1 327-4040 ($ = 182.5 Hungarian Forints)
